clue.text: Challenge sustained over years

indicators.note: over in a down-or-across clue can mean turned over, so the word for sustained is read backwards

parts.note: to sustain someone is to feed them, past tense fed

explanation.surface: A legal challenge has been kept going for years on end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns FED back to DEF before Y is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge an authority is to openly resist or flout it.

clue.text: Stupid individual takes the plunge on credit

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: dips means plunges into water
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: A fool dives in and buys on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' is British informal for credit, as in buying 'on tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipstick is informal slang for an idiot.

clue.text: Assume it's imported, perhaps, or exported

indicators.note: exported means sent out, so the word or is taken away

parts.note: imported goods come from abroad, so are foreign

explanation.surface: Guessing whether a product was brought in from abroad or sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exported' removes OR from FOREIGN; 'perhaps' marks imported things as one example of the foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume an air or attitude is to put it on, to pretend.

clue.text: Always receiving mail when abandoning principles

indicators.note: receiving means the word for always takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: AY (or aye) is an old word for always
mail is the post
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone who is forever opening letters at the moment they drop their ideals.
explanation.definitionFit: Renouncing a faith or cause one held is the very meaning of the noun, a defection from belief.

clue.text: Demonstrate right blade, at first, for a saw

parts.note: to demonstrate something is to prove it

indicators.note: at first means take only the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Show the correct blade for a cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the tool, matching 'blade', but means an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or maxim.

clue.text: Playing to the crowd?

parts.note: not showing off, but literally a game played for an audience of onlookers

explanation.definitionFit: A game such as football is one that draws large audiences to watch it.

clue.text: Outline faintly a pretty stupid charge

parts.note: dumb means stupid
a charge is a rate or price

explanation.surface: A rather foolish fee is being sketched out.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to sketch or foreshadow in vague terms.

clue.text: Suddenly pull new animal round

indicators.note: round means the animal goes round the letter for new

parts.note: a yak is a Tibetan ox

explanation.surface: A newly acquired beast is jerked around by its handler.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to tug sharply.

clue.text: One's report allows entrants to proceed

definitions.text: One's report allows entrants to proceed

parts.words: One's report allows entrants to proceed
parts.note: report here is the bang of a gun, which signals runners in a race to set off

explanation.definitionFit: The gun fired to begin a race gives competitors their signal to run.

clue.text: Cricket side Robin possibly supports when not doing well

indicators.note: in a down clue, supports means the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
Robin Day was a famous British television interviewer

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder named Robin backs a struggling team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the off side is the half of the field facing the batter; Sir Robin Day was a famous BBC political interviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad day is when someone performs below their usual standard.

clue.text: Justification for lack of profit, perhaps, in a crisis

parts.note: the point of doing something is its justification
of can stand for 'for' in phrases like 'the point of it'
no profit is no return on an investment

explanation.surface: An excuse offered for a loss-making venture during an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags that the reading of the phrase as 'justification for no profit' is a playful one; 'in' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage after which there is no going back is a critical moment, a crisis point.

clue.text: Tried bong, getting stoned in market town

indicators.note: getting stoned suggests the letters are knocked out of their sober order and jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone tried a bong and got high in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stoned' rearranges TRIED BONG. TONBRIDGE is a market town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a Kentish town with a long-established weekly market.

clue.text: Only backing English TV?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for only is read in reverse

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A complaint that television offers nothing but English programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns BUT into TUB; the question mark marks the definition as slang, 'the tube' being American slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, the tube is the television set, from its old cathode-ray screen.

clue.text: Something offensive heard in team song?

indicators.note: heard signals that the phrase is spoken and the answer is what it sounds like

parts.note: a rowing team is a crew and a song is a ditty

explanation.surface: A rude line overheard in a sports team's chant.
explanation.walkthrough: A crew is a rowing team; 'crew ditty' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crudity is a vulgar remark or act, something coarse that may offend.

clue.text: Like some officers, in ignorance, missing a point

indicators.note: missing means the letter for a compass point is dropped

parts.note: someone in ignorance is not informed
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Some officers are clueless and missing the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers in regulation dress, as opposed to plain clothes, are in uniform.

clue.text: Attendant appears a comic character

definitions.meaning: the caped superhero of DC comics

explanation.definitionFit: An officer's orderly bears this title, and so does the masked crime-fighter from Gotham.

clue.text: Glowing review of how the desired quality is injected

indicators.note: is injected means the desired quality goes inside the rearranged letters
review here means look at again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: IT is the undefinable appeal everyone wants, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: A rave write-up of how a sought-after quality was added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review of' rearranges HOW THE into WHEHOT, and 'is injected' puts IT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal heated until it glows white is hotter than red-hot.

clue.text: Someone complaining at sending off of hard footballer

indicators.note: sending off means removing, so the letter for hard is dropped from the complainer

parts.note: a whinger is a persistent moaner
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A player moans at a tough-tackling footballer being sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending off' sounds like a referee's red card but here strips H from WHINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger is a footballer who plays out wide on the flank.

clue.text: The title's possible that's for sure!

definitions.meaning: the title 'Right Hon', for Right Honourable, said with a silent h

explanation.walkthrough: A British cabinet minister is styled 'the Right Honourable', shortened to 'Rt Hon'; the h in Hon is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal exclamation of agreement, and also how the title Rt Hon is spoken.

clue.text: Yell from companion on loose rock

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the companion comes after the rock

parts.note: scree is loose stones on a mountainside
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A climber shouts as a friend scrambles over loose stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a loud piercing cry, a shriek or yell.

clue.text: Returned some stolen mistletoe, and the cake

indicators.note: Returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone gave back stolen Christmas mistletoe along with a festive bake.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'and the cake' includes the link 'and the'; only 'cake' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Simnel is a fruit cake topped with marzipan, eaten around Easter.

clue.text: One marshy area turned into desert

indicators.note: turned means the letters for one and the marsh are read backwards together

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a bog is a marsh

explanation.surface: A swamp that dried out and became desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses I + BOG to give the answer; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the great arid expanse spanning Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Chance to secure part of a set

definitions.text: Chance to secure part of a set

parts.words: Chance to secure part of a set
parts.note: in tennis a set is made of games, and this is the moment a player can win the next one

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the score at which a player needs one more rally to win a game, a unit of a set.

clue.text: Head off champion aiming for gold, not quite there

definitions.text: aiming for gold, not quite there

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the champion is removed

parts.note: a champion is a winner

explanation.surface: An athlete chasing a gold medal falls just short of the title.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery the gold is the bullseye; the ring just outside it is the inner.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery target the ring next to the central gold is a near miss.

clue.text: About to interrupt broadcast describing a boat

indicators.note: to interrupt means the letter for about cuts into the other word

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone about to break into a radio show about a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed barge.

clue.text: Reach critical point, and start to chew things over?

definitions.meaning: read literally, get to the stage of biting and crunching food

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means reaching the decisive moment, and read literally it means starting to munch noisily.

clue.text: Proceeding awkwardly with sum left in first of GCSEs

parts.note: to sum is to add
taken as written

indicators.note: first of picks out just the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A student doing badly with maths after failing the first of their exams.
explanation.walkthrough: GCSEs are the exams English pupils sit at about sixteen; only its first letter G is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To waddle is to walk with a clumsy rocking gait, moving forward ungracefully.

clue.text: Worry that guitarist may press on?

definitions.meaning: a ridge on a guitar neck that fingers press strings against

explanation.definitionFit: To be anxious is to fret, and a fret is one of the metal bars on a guitar fingerboard.
